m.chalisa.do1: Bowing my head to the Arihantas, I offer salutation to the Siddhas, and take the joy-giving names of the Upādhyāyas and Ācāryas.
m.chalisa.do2: Bowing too to all the sādhus, to Sarasvatī and to the joy-giving Jina temples, I hold Lord Mahāvīra in the temple of my mind.
m.chalisa.cau1: Victory to you, Mahāvīra, merciful Lord. Lord Vīra, you are renowned in the world.
m.chalisa.cau2: Vardhamāna is your name; it feels most dear to the heart.
m.chalisa.cau3: Your image is peaceful and your form enchanting; your lovely face is full of dignity and smiling.
m.chalisa.cau4: You took the sky-clad guise of a digambara; even the enemy karma was defeated by you.
m.chalisa.cau5: You drove away anger, pride and greed; great delusion grew afraid of you.
m.chalisa.cau6: You are omniscient, the knower of all; what bond have you with the world?
m.chalisa.cau7: In you there is neither attachment nor hatred; you are the hero in the battle with attachment, the teacher of what is good.
m.chalisa.cau8: Your name in the world is true, a name every child knows.
m.chalisa.cau9: Ghosts and spirits are afraid of you; vyantaras (wandering spirits) and demons all run away.
m.chalisa.cau10: Great sickness and plague cause no torment; Death, most dreadful, is afraid.
m.chalisa.cau11: Be it a black, hooded cobra, or a huge and fearsome lion,
m.chalisa.cau12: and should there be no one to save, then, Lord, you alone protect.
m.chalisa.cau13: Should a forest fire be smouldering and blazing up in a strong wind,
m.chalisa.cau14: your name takes away all sorrow, and the fire turns cool at once.
m.chalisa.cau15: All Bhārata was full of violence; then you brought it deliverance.
m.chalisa.cau16: You were born in the city of Kuṇḍalapura; then all the people were happy.
m.chalisa.cau17: Siddhārtha was your father; you were the apple of Triśalā's eye.
m.chalisa.cau18: Leaving all worldly entanglements, the Lord became a celibate from boyhood.
m.chalisa.cau19: In the fifth age, a time of great sorrow, you showed your glory at Cāṁdanapura.
m.chalisa.cau20: In a mound you showed a wonder (atiśaya): you made a cow's milk flow there.
m.chalisa.cau21: Worry arose in the cowherd's mind; he came there with a spade.
m.chalisa.cau22: He dug away the whole mound and cast it aside; then you gave your darśana.
m.chalisa.cau23: Trouble beset Jodharāja; when he chanted your name,
m.chalisa.cau24: the cannonball turned cold; then everyone raised the cry of victory.
m.chalisa.cau25: The minister had a temple built; the king too spent wealth on it.
m.chalisa.cau26: A large rest-house was built, and it was settled to bring you.
m.chalisa.cau27: You broke scores of carts; the wheel did not budge forward.
m.chalisa.cau28: When the cowherd put his hand to it, the chariot was then found moving.
m.chalisa.cau29: On the first day of the dark fortnight of Vaiśākha, the chariot goes to the bank of the river.
m.chalisa.cau30: The Mīṇās and Gujars all come; dancing and leaping, their hearts all swell with joy.
m.chalisa.cau31: Lord, you kept faith with love, and greatly raised the cowherd's honour.
m.chalisa.cau32: Only when the cowherd's hand touches it, Lord, does the chariot move.
m.chalisa.cau33: My boat is all but broken; without you there is no one to row it across.
m.chalisa.cau34: Lord, show me a little grace; I am your servant, Lord.
m.chalisa.cau35: I want nothing else from you; may I have your darśana birth after birth.
m.chalisa.cau36: Candra composes this Chālīsā and bows his head to Lord Vīra.
m.chalisa.so1: Whoever recites it forty times a day for forty days, burning fragrant incense without measure before Vardhamāna,
m.chalisa.so2: if he is poor from birth, becomes like Kubera; if he has no children, his name and line carry on in the world.
